fix_commit.message: rtmp: fix double-free on URL parse errors
fix_commit.author: Daniel Stenberg

findings.title: Double-free of RTMP* on URL parse failure in rtmp_setup_connection()
findings.message: rtmp_setup_connection() allocates an RTMP handle with RTMP_Alloc() and immediately registers it in the connection's meta hash via Curl_conn_meta_set(conn, CURL_META_RTMP_CONN, r, rtmp_conn_dtor). From this point on, ownership of `r` is effectively transferred to the connection meta store, which will invoke rtmp_conn_dtor() (calling RTMP_Close(r) and RTMP_Free(r)) automatically whenever the connection's meta data is torn down (e.g. when the connectdata is destroyed after a failed connection setup). However, if the subsequent RTMP_SetupURL(r, data->state.url) call fails (e.g. because of a malformed rtmp:// URL), the code still executes the old cleanup path RTMP_Free(r) directly before returning CURLE_URL_MALFORMAT. Because `r` remains registered in the connection meta hash (it was never removed via Curl_conn_meta_remove), when the connection is later destroyed the meta destructor rtmp_conn_dtor() runs again and calls RTMP_Free(r) (and RTMP_Close(r)) a second time on the same pointer, resulting in a double-free / use-after-free that can be triggered simply by supplying a malformed RTMP URL.
findings.suggestion: Do not call RTMP_Free(r) manually in the URL-parse-error path once `r` has been registered with Curl_conn_meta_set() and an rtmp_conn_dtor is attached. Either remove the meta entry (Curl_conn_meta_remove) before freeing manually, or simply let the connection meta destructor perform the cleanup and just return the error code without freeing.

ground_truth.root_cause: When ownership/lifetime management of the RTMP* was moved to the connection meta-data hash (with an automatic destructor), the pre-existing manual free on the URL-parse-error early-return path was not removed, leaving two independent code paths (the manual free and the meta destructor) that both free the same object.
